course.title: Time Series Analysis
course.prerequisites: Predictive Analytics or equivalent background in statistical analysis, regression modelling, and Python-based data processing
course.description: This course introduces fundamental and advanced concepts in time series analysis for forecasting and decision-making. Students will learn how to analyze temporal data using exploratory data analysis (EDA), decomposition, and stationarity techniques, followed by building forecasting models such as AR, MA, ARIMA, and SARIMA. The course emphasizes practical implementation using programming tools, where students develop skills in model construction, diagnostics, and performance evaluation. In addition, modern approaches including feature engineering, machine learning optimization, and hybrid models are introduced to enhance forecasting accuracy. Students will also learn how to validate models using appropriate techniques and deploy solutions using tools such as Streamlit and Kaggle notebook. The course culminates in a team-based project, where students collaboratively design, implement, and present a complete time series forecasting system. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyze, construct, evaluate, and communicate time series solutions applicable to real-world problems.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Time Series
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain key characteristics of time series data LLO2: Differentiate time series from cross-sectional data

topics.title: Topic 2: EDA & Visualization
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse trends and patterns in time series data LLO2: Visualize time series using appropriate plots

topics.title: Topic 3: Decomposition
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse trend, seasonality, and residual components LLO2: Interpret decomposed time series results

topics.title: Topic 4: Stationarity & ADF
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse stationarity in time series data LLO2: Apply ADF test to determine stationarity LLO3: Interpret ADF test results to determine appropriate transformations

topics.title: Topic 5: ACF & PACF
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation plots LLO2: Interpret ACF/PACF for model identification LLO3: Justify model order selection based on ACF and PACF patterns

topics.title: Topic 6: AR, MA, ARIMA
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain AR, MA, and ARIMA model structures LLO2: Construct appropriate models for time series data LLO3: Compare AR, MA, and ARIMA models for different scenarios

topics.title: Topic 7: ARIMA Implementation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Implement ARIMA models using software tools LLO2: Generate forecasts from trained models

topics.title: Topic 8: SARIMA
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Analyse seasonal patterns in time series data LLO2: Construct SARIMA models for seasonal data LLO3: Justify inclusion of seasonal components

topics.title: Topic 9: Diagnostics & Validation
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Evaluate residual diagnostics of models LLO2: Apply validation techniques to assess model performance LLO3: Interpret residual patterns to identify model issues

topics.title: Topic 10: Feature Engineering
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Construct lag and rolling features LLO2: Prepare datasets for ML models LLO3: Evaluate impact of features on performance

topics.title: Topic 11: ML Models for TS
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Apply machine learning models to time series data LLO2: Collaborate to develop forecasting solutions LLO3: Compare ML models with statistical approaches

topics.title: Topic 12: Model Comparison & Selection
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Evaluate model performance using validation metrics LLO2: Justify model selection based on results LLO3: Defend chosen model in discussion or presentation

topics.title: Topic 13: Final Project: Notebook Finalization & Model Export
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Organize analysis into a structured notebook LLO2: Communicate results clearly using markdown and visuals LLO3: Justify modelling decisions in the notebook

topics.title: Topic 14: Final Project: Streamlit Deployment
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Develop a simple application for time series outputs LLO2: Present deployed solution effectively LLO3: Explain system functionality and user interaction

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
